subject: red chili peppers
title: What If You Ate Spicy Food Every Day?

scenes.text: What if you ate spicy food every day? Your tongue isn't really burning. It's being fooled.
Capsaicin in chili switches on the same nerve sensor that warns you about heat above about 43 degrees Celsius.
That sensor mattered so much that its discovery won a Nobel Prize in 2021.
In a study of nearly half a million adults in China, eating spicy food almost daily was linked to a 14 percent lower risk of death.
It's a link, not proof. And the hottest peppers can backfire: one man got thunderclap headaches from a single Carolina Reaper.
So the burn is fake, and the benefit might be real. The record peppers are another story.

description:
What if you ate spicy food every day? Capsaicin activates TRPV1, the nerve sensor that also detects heat above about 43 C; its discovery earned David Julius the 2021 Nobel Prize.
The China Kadoorie Biobank study of 487,375 adults (BMJ, 2015) linked eating spicy food almost every day with a 14 percent lower risk of death (an association, not proof). A 2018 BMJ Case Report described thunderclap headaches after one Carolina Reaper.
